messages.content: Write a monthly engineering update for a team of twelve, covering a migration, two hires, and a slipped deadline. Around 200 words.

Here's a monthly update that reads like actual team communication:

---

**September Engineering Update**

We wrapped the database migration to PostgreSQL 16. The work took six weeks — longer than planned, but the async replication strategy we ended up using kept production stable throughout. Huge thanks to Sarah's crew on infrastructure; they caught a subtle index regression that would've hit us hard in October.

We're welcoming Raj and Marcus to the backend team next week. Raj joins from Stripe with deep experience in distributed systems; Marcus comes from a payments startup and already has ideas about our transaction pipeline.

On the deadline slip: the customer dashboard overhaul is moving to late October. We found that the current charting library can't handle our data volumes without serious rewrites, which cascades into the API changes we'd planned for this month. It's a blocker, not a pivot. We're scoping a different approach this week and will have real dates by Friday.

The team velocity has held steady despite the migration load. Incident count is down, and the on-call rotation has been smooth. We've got solid ground to build from as Q4 kicks off.

---

**193 words.** Specific names and timelines ground it; plain verbs and varied sentence length make it readable; the deadline slip is stated clearly without apology or hedging.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

output:
**September Engineering Update**

This month we completed the PostgreSQL 16 migration, which consumed six weeks of focused work. Running async replication throughout the migration kept the database available and responsive during the switchover process. Our infrastructure team identified an index regression during testing—a subtle issue that would have caused performance problems, but early detection prevented that from hitting production.

We're welcoming Raj and Marcus to the backend team starting next week. Raj spent seven years at Stripe working on distributed systems architecture; Marcus built payment platforms at his previous employer and is already reviewing our transaction pipeline for optimization opportunities.

The customer dashboard redesign shifts to late October instead of this month. The charting library we use can't handle our current data volumes without substantial work. We need to rewrite large parts of the visualization layer and modify the API contract. Having the extra time lets us explore different options and select an architecture that scales with our needs. We'll share updated schedules by Friday.

Despite the migration work, our team kept steady output. Incidents dropped, and the on-call rotation stayed reliable. Q4 looks manageable from here.
